issues.title: The classical-draw and optical-control denominators remain distinct
issues.quote: This family can display a same-circuit twofold success ratio, yet the classical uniform feasible control has success $\eta^2/3$ and a known-optimum identity control has success $\eta^2$.
issues.analysis: This is the unresolved local naming/denominator issue PN-F002 from v1, now rechecked in the fresh v2 context. Eta^2/3 is correct for uniform feasible strings prepared as two-photon optical states and sent through the same survival/readout model, as in P40. The standalone classical balanced sampler succeeds with2/6=1/3 per classical draw independently of optical transmission. At eta=1/2 these are1/12 per optical injected attempt versus1/3 per classical draw. The benchmark section uses the classical uniform sampler as an algorithmic feasibility baseline, so the pilot sentence should explicitly identify its added optical preparation and loss stage. No P40 identity is rejected and no algorithmic-advantage claim is alleged.
issues.suggested_fix: Name the eta^2/3 comparator a classically selected feasible-state optical control under the common loss/readout channel, and separately state1/3 per draw for the standalone classical sampler. Keep the frozen P40 optical prediction.

issues.title: The rejection bucket does determine the bosonic pair moment at k=2
issues.location: paper/sections/05_experiments.tex:15; compare paper/sections/03_certificate.tex:eq:moment and the n4,k2 benchmark domain
issues.quote: The simulator retains the total non-CF mass as an explicit rejection category, without resolving its internal collision histogram; the E05b traces therefore cannot estimate the pair moment $M$.
issues.analysis: The blanket cannot-estimate statement includes n=4,k=n/2=2. For every fixed two-photon occupation t, sum_i binom(t_i,2)=1_{t not in CF}: each non-CF event has exactly one doubled mode, while every CF event has zero pairs. Consequently the bosonic M=1-P_CF is estimable from that rejection bucket alone in the n4 arms; no internal collision histogram is needed. A bounded exact check of all ten m4,k2 occupations confirmed the pathwise identity. In contrast, k3 occupations(3,0,0,0) and(2,1,0,0) both fall in the bucket but carry3 and1 pairs. Thus the insufficiency is real in general for k>=3, not for the full stated size grid. This does not make finite-shot density certification automatic: the density floor and uncertainties remain separate.
issues.suggested_fix: Restrict the insufficiency to the general k>=3 case (the n6,n8 optical arms), and note that at n4,k2 the rejected fraction estimates the bosonic pair moment directly. Do not extend the Fock-moment statement to Bernoulli penalty arms.

issues.title: The new density caption double-escapes the envelope macro
issues.location: paper/sections/05_experiments.tex:33, caption of fig:density; compare eq:envelope in paper/sections/03_certificate.tex
issues.quote: \caption{Left: 300 complete-law grid checks against the coarse density envelope $\\Phi(M/c)$ from the accepted supervised primary/replication archive.
issues.analysis: The immutable v2 source contains bytes92,92,80,104,105 before the caption envelope argument: two backslashes followed by Phi. The defined mathematical envelope is the single-backslash command Phi. The doubled sequence is a TeX line-break command followed by letters, not the intended envelope macro. This is a source-level caption slip only; no PDF rendering or failed build is asserted. Ref/cref in the newly added method paragraph were separately checked and have the correct single slash.
issues.suggested_fix: Use one backslash before Phi in the fig:density math expression. Leave the coarse quantity M/c and its mathematical meaning unchanged.
